text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein expresses his desire that Palestinian-Israeli talks at Erez border crossing lead to definite solutions to problems facing the two sides.
- Crown Prince says during his visit to the Bani-Hamida tribes that "no injustice will touch anyone living in King Hussein's Jordan."
- Fifty seven thousand new telephone lines in the city of Irbid by end of 1998.
- An integrated project to develop the eastern coast of the Dead Sea with health, public beaches and tourist villages, with the infrastructure costs estimated at 65 million dinars ($91 million).
- Islamists and leftists join in first ever coalition ticket in the coming engineers union club elections.

- U.S. State department spokesman says King Hussein is the voice of reason in the peace process and played a leading role in the Washington summit; Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu pledges to U.S. President Clinton to implement the Oslo accord.
- The council of minister's legal department discusses the draft new securities law that incorporates a new watchdog regulatory body.
- Crown Prince phones king and Egyptian President Mubarak to discuss "Arab coordination to ensure success of Israeli-Palestinian talks."
- Cabinet approves Japanese loan to the kingdom to purchase $373,000 worth of appliances for tourism ministry.
- Jordan's national airline carrier, Royal Jordanian (RJ), says 26,000 European tourists cancelled their bookings on chartered flights due to political uncertainty in the region.
- Kuwaiti deputy foreign minister Shaheen says Kuwait is giving priority to normalising ties with Jordan.
- Crown Prince says the "call of Jerusalem" sent King Hussein to Washington.
